# testdata

Captured artefacts this crate's own tests read. **Not `fixtures/`**: nothing
here is oracle data, nothing here is an expected value produced by a reference,
and `superset-check.py` has no business with it. These are inputs — recordings
of what an older version of *our* code wrote, kept so a compatibility path can
be exercised against the real thing instead of against a test's idea of it.

| file | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `keystore_v1_snapshot.bin` | An `accounts.mks` written by the format-version-1 encoder at commit `2e3fbe0`, the last commit before version 2 existed: `Keystore::create` then two `add`s — an imported root `0xB7 * 32` under the tag `0x1A * 20` (v1's `import_with_unverified_tag`, since removed) and `F-derive-account-1`. 242 bytes = `22 + 2*94 + 32`. Read by `src/keystore/format.rs`'s version-dispatch test and by `tests/keystore.rs::a_version_1_store_is_refused_with_upgrade_not_damage`; one copy, embedded twice, so the two cannot drift. Errata 163, 164. |
| `keystore_v2_snapshot.bin` | An `accounts.mks` written by the format-version-2 encoder at commit `8062c9a`, the last commit whose encoder wrote v2 (W1-14 replaced it at `0c07b65`): `Keystore::create` then two `add`s of the harness's own accounts, `imported_account()` (`F-address-widths`, tag `05ff…800f`) and `derived_account()` (`F-derive-account-1`, tag `4d9b…fbe9`), in the C-free configuration in a scratch worktree (P10, errata 209). 410 bytes = `22 + 2*178 + 32`; sha256 `590b2083…8520`. The imported record sorts first, so bytes 22..42 are its tag and byte 42 its kind, `1` — which is what `format::older_first_account` reads and what the version refusal names (errata 207). Read by `src/keystore/format.rs`'s version-dispatch test and by `tests/keystore.rs::the_version_refusal_names_the_refused_stores_first_account_and_how_to_compare_it`; one copy, embedded twice, so the two cannot drift. Until P10 the format test built its "v2" arm by forging the v1 file's version word and said no v2 encoder was left to capture one with; the encoder is in git history, and this file is what it wrote. |
| `keystore_v3_snapshot.bin` | An `accounts.mks` written by the format-version-3 encoder **at `Kdf::RECOMMENDED` (65536/3/1)** by the build of the commit that added this row (`git log --follow` on the file names it; P5, errata 196): `Keystore::create`, `adopt_master`, `add(Account::derive(master, 0))` — what `cli::create::create` writes once the phrase has become a seed — under the fixed password, salt, nonce seed and master that `tests/keystore.rs::a_store_sealed_by_an_earlier_build_opens_and_is_reproduced_byte_for_byte` spells out. 290 bytes = `51 + (45 + 178) + 16`. Captured by an out-of-tree program depending on the crate by path in the C-free configuration (the sealed path never reaches the backend, errata 152); the test runs in both configurations and requires each to reproduce the bytes. **It is a pin of this build against its own past, not an oracle**: it says nothing about correctness (the RFC 9106 anchor does) and is never re-captured to make a red green — a re-captured file certifies whatever broke it. Re-capture only after a deliberate format change recorded in the errata, keeping this file under its version -- **which P13 did** (errata 213 §4, 214): version 4 is what this build writes, this file is kept byte for byte, and its subject is now the version-3 READ PATH at the shipped parameter point (arm 1 of the pin test), with the byte-for-byte arm moved to the v4 pin below. |
| `keystore_v4_snapshot.bin` | An `accounts.mks` written by the format-version-4 encoder **at `Kdf::RECOMMENDED` (65536/3/1)** by the build of the commit that added this row (P13, errata 214): the same three calls as the v3 pin -- `Keystore::create`, `adopt_master`, `add(Account::derive(master, 0))` -- under the same fixed password, salt, nonce seed and master, by an out-of-tree program depending on the crate by path in the C-free configuration. 307 bytes = `51 + (45 + 195) + 16`; sha256 `828fcf6f…103c`. It is arm 2 of `tests/keystore.rs::a_store_sealed_by_an_earlier_build_opens_and_is_reproduced_byte_for_byte`: this build must reproduce it byte for byte. Like the v3 pin on the day it was captured, it pins nothing until the next commit. Same rule: never re-captured to make a red green. |
| `keystore_v3_reserved_snapshot.bin` | An `accounts.mks` written by the format-version-3 encoder at commit `529017f`, the last commit whose encoder wrote v3, **with a reservation open** and at `Kdf::CHEAP_FOR_TESTS` (8/1/1): `Keystore::create` under the harness's fixed password, salt and nonce seed, `adopt_master` (`F-address-widths`' master, `IMPORTED_MASTER`), `add(Account::derive(master, 0))` (tag `05ff…800f`, `IMPORTED_TAG`), then `persist_advance(&tag, &[0xD1; 32])` -- the two-argument signature of that build -- in a scratch worktree, the way P10 captured the v2 file (P13, errata 213 §4, 214). 290 bytes = `51 + (45 + 178) + 16`; sha256 `b4d14a9b…8231`; generation 3, index 1, a reservation at 0, no figures anywhere in it. It is the real file behind the declared-absent arm of the migration: read under Miri by `src/keystore/format.rs`'s version-dispatch test and by its malformation table's `v3_state_2` row (one Argon2 at the cheap point -- errata 184 -- and a derived record, so no WOTS+ generation), and through the public `open` by `tests/keystore.rs::a_version_3_reservation_is_read_with_its_figures_absent_and_still_resigns`, `tests/recon.rs::a_migrated_reservation_declines_to_classify` and `tests/cli.rs::a_migrated_store_says_its_figures_were_not_recorded_and_is_resealed_by_its_first_write`. A captured input of ours, not oracle data; never edited. |
